appearance_facts.fact: Title text reads 'Product Rating Share by Category'.
Vertical axis labeled 'Value' with tick marks from 0 to 55 in increments of 5.
Horizontal axis labeled 'Category' with six category labels: Quality, Price, Design, Support, Delivery, Other.
Six blue circular markers are plotted, each with a percentage label directly above it.
The 'Design' marker is positioned highest on the chart, followed by 'Other', 'Delivery', 'Price', 'Quality', and 'Support' from top to bottom.

printed_facts.fact: Label '36%' is printed above the Quality marker.
Label '38%' is printed above the Price marker.
Label '34%' is printed above the Design marker.
Label '45%' is printed above the Support marker.
Label '43%' is printed above the Delivery marker.
Label '53%' is printed above the Other marker.

public_definitions: Task: 'Review the Product Rating Share dashboard, then assign additional promotional budget to the category with the highest current labeled rating share.'
Policy: 'Select the category with the highest current labeled rating share'
Evidence source: 'Use the dashboard labeled rating-share values as the evidence source'
uncertain: The visual height of the 'Design' marker (approx. 54) contradicts its printed label '34%'. The task requires using 'labeled rating-share values', so the printed text is the authoritative source, but the visual discrepancy is noted.
The visual height of the 'Support' marker (approx. 30) contradicts its printed label '45%'. Again, the printed label is treated as the source of truth per instructions.
